'''Jean Jacod''' (born 13 November 1944)<ref>{{cite web |title=CURRICULUM VITAE de Jean JACOD |url=http://www.univ-orleans.fr/mapmo/membres/anker/documents/CMCU2014/CV/CVjacod2013.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806085159/http://www.univ-orleans.fr/mapmo/membres/anker/documents/CMCU2014/CV/CVjacod2013.pdf |archive-date=6 August 2018 |access-date=14 July 2022}}</ref> is a [[French people|French]] [[mathematician]] specializing in stochastic processes and probability theory. He has been a professor at the [[Université Pierre et Marie Curie]].<ref name="Laboratoire de Probabilités, Statistique et Modélisation (LPSM, UMR 8001)">{{cite web | title=Jean Jacod | website=Laboratoire de Probabilités, Statistique et Modélisation (LPSM, UMR 8001) | url=https://www.lpsm.paris/pageperso/jacod/ | language=fr | access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref>
He has made fundamental contributions to a wide range of topics in probability theory including [[stochastic calculus]], [[Central limit theorem|limit theorems]], martingale problems, [[Malliavin calculus]]
and statistics of [[stochastic processes]].

==Biography==

Jean Jacod graduated from [[Ecole Polytechnique]] in 1965 and obtained his [[Doctorat d'État]] in Mathematics from the Université Paris-VI. His advisor was [[Jacques Neveu]].

* J. JACOD, Z. KOWALSKI, [[Ashkan Nikeghbali|A. NIKEGHBALI]]: Mod-Gaussian convergence: new limit theorems in probability and number theory. Forum Math. 23, 835-873 (2011).
